comparisons.title: Sumo Smash! vs Sumo Battle!
comparisons.excerpt: Two sumo games with the same growth idea and different priorities: arena chests and skins versus a simpler body-mass push.
comparisons.intro: Both games ask you to eat, grow and push an opponent out of the ring. The difference is what surrounds that loop: Sumo Smash! adds arena chests and skins, while Sumo Battle! keeps the focus on body mass and the podium.
comparisons.pickA: Pick Sumo Smash! if you want a slightly busier arena with chests, skins and a clearer party-game tone.
comparisons.pickB: Pick Sumo Battle! if you want the simpler version: eat sushi, gain size, push, repeat, with less around the edges.
comparisons.verdict: They are close enough that the theme and lobby decide it. Start with Sumo Smash! for the extra collectibles; choose Sumo Battle! for a cleaner push loop.

comparisons.title: Snake VS AI vs Grab.io
comparisons.excerpt: Two territory games: one is a single-player rank climb with snake trails, the other is a faster paper.io-style land grab against bots.
comparisons.intro: Both ask you to leave home, draw a loop and return without touching a trail. Snake VS AI adds a rank ladder, AI personalities and an Unlimited mode; Grab.io keeps the round short and the arena round.
comparisons.pickA: Pick Snake VS AI if you want a single-player progression arc, unlockable snake skins and a mode that removes the timer.
comparisons.pickB: Pick Grab.io if you want the cleaner paper.io loop: leave land, close the loop, dodge every trail, repeat.
comparisons.verdict: Snake VS AI is the better long-session package. Grab.io is the better “one quick round” pick if you do not care about ranks.

comparisons.title: Duckling Rush.io vs Ducklings.io
comparisons.excerpt: Two duck collection games with different pressures: a 90-second competitive dash versus a calmer nest-building rescue loop.
comparisons.intro: The theme is the same; the session is not. Duckling Rush.io is a timed pond race with rival mamas and a QUACK burst. Ducklings.io is a slower rescue-and-upgrade loop with boats as the main hazard.
comparisons.pickA: Pick Duckling Rush.io if you want a short competitive round with stealing, bursts and a clear 90-second finish.
comparisons.pickB: Pick Ducklings.io if you want a calmer collection game where the goal is a better nest rather than beating a rival.
comparisons.verdict: Choose by mood, not by theme. Rush is the arcade pick; Ducklings is the wind-down pick.

comparisons.title: Yolk Ops Egg Arena vs Block Team Deathmatch
comparisons.excerpt: Two solo-friendly browser shooters: an egg-themed arena with AI bots versus a pixel-block FPS with team, individual and sniper modes.
comparisons.intro: Both are first-person shooters that can be played without a live lobby, but they solve the population problem differently. Yolk Ops is explicit about being single-player against bots. Block Team Deathmatch offers team, individual and sniper modes, with team mode recommended first.
comparisons.pickA: Pick Yolk Ops if you want a complete solo arena package with eight maps, three modes and a clear bot count.
comparisons.pickB: Pick Block Team Deathmatch if you want a blocky FPS with team modes and a progression recommendation for new players.
comparisons.verdict: Yolk Ops is the safer solo recommendation. Block Team Deathmatch is the better fit if you want team modes and do not mind learning by playing.
